issues.description: push_error called with a string but expects an ErrorFrame
issues.detail: In pipecat, push_error typically expects an ErrorFrame instance, not a raw string keyword. The original code used `error_msg=` which suggests a helper, but verify push_error's signature — passing a plain string where a Frame is expected will raise at runtime. This regression-prone change should be confirmed against the base class.

The tuple of error message types lists 'transcriber_error' twice (lines ~725 and ~731). Harmless functionally but indicates a copy-paste slip and suggests the list was not carefully reviewed against ElevenLabs docs. Deduplicate and double-check no intended type was dropped.

issues.description: Loss of error-level logging for error frames
issues.detail: Previously each error branch called `logger.error(...)` before pushing. The consolidated branch only pushes the error frame and no longer logs at error level, making upstream debugging harder when push_error is filtered or swallowed. Add a `logger.error` before push_error to preserve observability.

issues.description: Broad except inside _receive_messages may still suppress disconnects
issues.detail: The inner `except Exception as e: logger.error(...)` inside the `async for` loop will still catch a websocket disconnect exception raised during iteration if it surfaces via json.loads/_process_response, potentially masking the disconnect the PR aims to surface. Consider narrowing to JSONDecodeError or letting websocket errors propagate.
`changelog/3233.fixed.md` ends without a trailing newline ("No newline at end of file"). Minor POSIX/style nit; many lint configs and changelog aggregators expect a terminal newline.

issues.description: Generic error label loses type context downstream
issues.detail: All error variants now produce `f"Error: {error_msg}"` with no message_type prefix in the pushed frame. Previously auth/quota errors had distinguishing prefixes. Downstream consumers can no longer differentiate auth vs quota vs rate_limited without parsing the payload. Include message_type in the pushed error string.

review.summary: The PR correctly addresses the infinite-loop risk by removing the swallowing try/except in `_receive_messages` and expands recognized error message types. Main concerns: a duplicated `transcriber_error` entry, loss of explicit `logger.error` logging for error events, and loss of per-type error labeling in pushed frames. The inner `except Exception` inside the message loop may still mask the very disconnect this PR is trying to surface. Minor changelog newline nit.
